name: Pearl Bailey
description: Pearl Bailey was an American singer and actress born March 29, 1918, in Newport News, Virginia, and raised in part in Philadelphia, where she left high school at fifteen for a career as a singer and dancer. She sang in cafes, nightclubs and theatres, at times with big bands led by Cootie Williams and Count Basie, and joined Cab Calloway for theatre and nightclub engagements after a 1944–45 stint at New York's Blue Angel. Her Broadway debut came in St. Louis Woman in 1946 and her first film, Variety Girl, in 1947. She took secondary film roles in Carmen Jones (1954) and Porgy and Bess (1959). Her most memorable stage role was Dolly Gallagher Levi in the all-Black production of Hello, Dolly!, on Broadway from 1967 to 1969 and then on tour. She received a Special Tony Award for that title role in 1968. She hosted The Pearl Bailey Show in 1971, was appointed a special ambassador to the United Nations in 1975, earned a Georgetown bachelor's degree in theology at sixty-seven, and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Ronald Reagan in 1988. She died August 17, 1990, in Philadelphia.

name: ProQuest Historical Black Newspapers
description: ProQuest Historical Black Newspapers is the dominant commercial digitization program for historic Black newspapers, offering full-page images and searchable text through institutional subscriptions rather than direct consumer access. CTL preservation research stresses the consequence: the Chicago Defender's backfile is reachable mainly through this paywall, its digitized edition is the national rather than the Chicago city edition, and the public these newspapers document largely cannot read them — digitized is not the same as publicly preserved.

name: Patricia E. Bath
description: Patricia Era Bath (1942-2019): Harlem-born ophthalmologist, laser scientist, inventor, and humanitarian. First African American to complete an ophthalmology residency (NYU, 1970-1973); first woman ophthalmologist on the UCLA medical school faculty (Jules Stein Eye Institute, 1974); co-founded the American Institute for the Prevention of Blindness (1976) and pioneered community ophthalmology. Developed the Laserphaco probe (device completed 1986 after laser research in Berlin) and was awarded U.S. Patent 4,744,360 on May 17, 1988 - the first U.S. medical patent awarded to an African American woman. First woman to head a U.S. ophthalmology residency program (King-Drew-UCLA, 1983). Inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame in 2022 (among the first Black women inductees). Died May 30, 2019, in San Francisco.

name: Percy Lavon Julian
description: Percy Lavon Julian (1899-1975): research chemist and pioneer in the chemical synthesis of medicinal drugs from plants. Born in Montgomery, Alabama, the grandson of slaves; first in his family to attend college (DePauw B.A. 1920; Harvard M.S. 1923; Vienna Ph.D. 1931). First to synthesize physostigmine, the glaucoma drug (1935). Denied faculty posts, he spent 18 years as Glidden's director of research (Soya Products Division), developing soy-protein fire-fighting foam used by the Navy in WWII and intermediates for synthetic progesterone, testosterone, and cortisone. Left Glidden in 1953; established Julian Laboratories (sold 1961, making him one of the first Black millionaires); founded the nonprofit Julian Research Institute (1964). First African American chemist elected to the National Academy of Sciences (1973). Held over 130 patents. Died of liver cancer in Waukegan, Illinois, April 19, 1975. PBS NOVA's 'Forgotten Genius'; USPS commemorative stamp, 1993.

name: Pullman sleeping car porters
description: Black railroad service workers employed by the Chicago-based Pullman Company to prepare, maintain, and operate sleeping cars across the U.S. rail network, c. 1870-1968. The Pullman Palace Car Company (est. 1867; Pullman Company from 1900) was the largest employer of African Americans -- some 12,000 Black workers by the 1920s -- while barring them from conductor jobs and paying porters low wages for long hours. On August 25, 1925 the porters organized the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters under A. Philip Randolph, the first predominantly Black labor union; after a twelve-year struggle it won the first collective bargaining agreement ever secured by a Black union (1937).

name: Pullman porter distribution network

name: Prince Hall Masons

Renamed Prince Hall Grand Lodge in 1847. In Illinois, North Star Lodge was organized in Chicago in 1852 (Ohio jurisdiction); with lodges in Alton (1856) and Springfield (1857) it formed the Prince Hall Grand Lodge for the State of Illinois in 1867. Headquarters: 809 E 42nd Place, Chicago. A major civic, charitable, and networking institution for Black Chicago.

name: Parliament
description: Parliament is an American funk band that began in 1955 as the Parliaments, a doo-wop vocal group rehearsing in a Plainfield, New Jersey barbershop under George Clinton. The group scored a hit with “(I Wanna) Testify” in 1967, but a contractual dispute cost Clinton the name; he relaunched the singers as Parliament on Invictus Records in 1970, shelved the name, then revived it at Casablanca Records in 1974 as the horn-driven, R&B-oriented counterpart to Funkadelic — two distinct bands sharing members and one leader. Mothership Connection (1975) built the group's Afrofuturist mythology; “Flash Light” (1978) became the P-Funk collective's first R&B number one, and “Aqua Boogie” also topped the chart that year. Clinton wound the band down after 1980 before reviving the name in 2018. description: Chicago radio personality and mix-show host whose voice carried house music and hip-hop across the South Side from WKKC 89.3 FM, the Kennedy-King College station in Englewood. Born Isadore Pink, he joined WKKC as host of Friday Night Audio — the station's Friday mix show, described by its own DJs as Chicago's longest-running radio mixshow, where a young crew including DJ Lil' John, Walter 'Get Down' Brown, and Bobby Q Bobby played the best that house music had to offer — and dubbed himself Pink House. A surviving summer 1987 aircheck catches him on the microphone beside Brown, throwing out his signature call: 'You Know It.' Block Club Chicago's history of the station names 'the late DJ Pink House,' with Mike Dunn and Sam Sylk, among the names that defined the 1980s and 1990s in local radio, on a station that brought house music to the masses, introduced Chicago house to generations of househeads, and gave local hip-hop artists life-changing airtime. Fake Shore Drive calls PinkHouse 'one of, if not, the most important figures in Chi rap history'; Chicago's DJ Summit named its Hip Hop Humanitarian Award for Isadore Pink; and Chris Casino's 2011 documentary Do You Remember preserves his story on film.

name: Plessy v. Ferguson decided (1896)
aliases: Plessy v. Ferguson; Separate But Equal; 'Separate But Equal'
description: On May 18, 1896, the United States Supreme Court decided Plessy v. Ferguson, 163 U.S. 537, upholding Louisiana's Separate Car Act and giving constitutional sanction to the doctrine the intake timeline names 'Separate But Equal.' The case was a planned test: Homer Plessy, a New Orleans shoemaker of mixed ancestry, boarded a whites-only railway car on June 7, 1892, and was arrested, in an action arranged with the Comité des Citoyens to challenge the law. The Court ruled 7–1 that segregated facilities did not violate the Fourteenth Amendment so long as they were equal — a condition the Jim Crow South honored almost nowhere. Justice John Marshall Harlan's lone dissent declared that the Constitution is color-blind. For fifty-eight years Plessy stood as the legal architecture of American apartheid, cited to defend segregation in schools, transport, housing, and public life, until Brown v. Board of Education (CTL-E-1540) dismantled its core in 1954. CTL records the decision as the doctrine's founding document: the case that made segregation a national legal language.

name: Pastor John F. Hannah
description: John F. Hannah is a Chicago-born pastor, author, and former gospel radio broadcaster — thirteen years on the air, by his published biographies — who founded New Life Covenant Church Southeast on the city's South Side and serves as its lead pastor. His ministry is built on prayer: 4 AM prayer gatherings, twelve-hour prayer events, prayer calls drawing thousands, and the annual Prayer on the 9 march for peace and development along 79th Street. In September 2021 he led his congregation into The Temple, a 100,000-square-foot, 4,000-seat worship and performing-arts center at 7621 South Greenwood Avenue, deliberately planted as an economic catalyst in Greater Grand Crossing. He is the author of Just Pray (2021), What to Do While You're Waiting, and Desperate for Jesus.

name: Pastor T.L. Barrett
aliases: T.L. Barrett; Thomas Lee Barrett Jr.; Rev. T.L. Barrett; Pastor T. L. Barrett and the Youth for Christ Choir
description: Thomas Lee Barrett Jr. (born January 13, 1944, in Jamaica, Queens, New York) is a Chicago pastor with a double legacy: a half-century pulpit career and a small catalog of 1970s gospel recordings that became canonical. Raised on Chicago's South Side, he began pastoring in 1966, led Mt. Zion Baptist Church in Washington Park from 1968, and left in 1976 to found the Life Center Church of God in Christ in the same neighborhood. Recording as Pastor T.L. Barrett and the Youth for Christ Choir — a roughly forty-voice ensemble of teenagers — he released Like a Ship (Without a Sail) in 1971 and further albums including Do Not Pass Me By (1976); his congregations included Maurice White, Philip Bailey, Donny Hathaway, and Phil Cohran. Reissued to acclaim from 2010, his work was sampled by Kanye West on The Life of Pablo (2016) and collected in the box set I Shall Wear a Crown (2021). Chicago named a stretch of Garfield Boulevard for him, and the Illinois House honored him in 1998. In 1989 Barrett was charged over a church economic-development fundraising scheme; a court ordered repayment of $1.2 million, which he completed by 1998.

name: Patrick Beverley
aliases: Pat Beverley; Pat Bev; Mr. 94 Feet
description: Patrick Beverley (born July 12, 1988, in Chicago, Illinois) is an American professional basketball guard who built a twelve-season NBA career on defense after taking the longest road to get there. Raised in West Garfield Park on Chicago's West Side, he attended Waubonsie Valley before transferring to John Marshall Metropolitan High School, where as a senior he led Illinois in scoring at 37.3 points per game. At Arkansas (2006–2008) he was the SEC Freshman of the Year, but an academic-integrity suspension ended his college career, and he turned professional overseas — Ukraine, Greece, and Russia, winning the EuroCup MVP award in 2012. Drafted 42nd overall by the Los Angeles Lakers in 2009, he reached the NBA with Houston in January 2013 and became a three-time All-Defensive Team selection and the league's first Hustle Award winner. In February 2023 he signed with his hometown Chicago Bulls for the remainder of the season, before later stops in Philadelphia and Milwaukee, and a return overseas.

name: Podcast P with Paul George
description: Podcast P with Paul George is a weekly basketball and culture podcast hosted by NBA forward Paul George with co-hosts Jackie Long and Dallas Rutherford. Announced by Wave Sports + Entertainment, the show released its first episode in March 2023 and built its format around George's first-person account of life in the league — training, injuries, matchups, and the business of basketball — mixed with guest interviews from across sports and entertainment. The show grew a substantial video audience alongside its audio feed: trade coverage in June 2024 reported roughly 720,000 YouTube subscribers, and Listen Notes counted 105 episodes by October 2026. CultureTechLens profiled Podcast P in Short #84, published October 13, 2026; no entity record existed before this packet.

name: P-Valley
description: P-Valley is a STARZ drama series created by Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright Katori Hall, set at The Pynk, a strip club in the fictional Mississippi Delta town of Chucalissa. Hall began the story in 2009 as the stage play Pussy Valley, built from interviews with more than forty dancers; the series premiered on STARZ in 2020 with Nicco Annan as the club's proprietor, Uncle Clifford. Its second season in 2022 averaged more than ten million viewers per episode across platforms, and the series has accumulated more than 236 million hours watched. Hall chose to end the series with its third season — nine episodes premiering December 4, 2026, the first two directed by Hall herself — writing to fans that ending on her own terms was the rarest honor a showrunner can have. CultureTechLens covered the final season in Short #139, published October 14, 2026.

name: Professor Griff
description: Professor Griff (born Richard Duane Griffin on August 1, 1960, on Long Island, New York) was Public Enemy's Minister of Information — the role, unique in hip-hop, that made research and ideology a named seat in a rap group. An Army veteran, Griffin ran a security firm, Unity Force, which he converted into the S1W, the uniformed Security of the First World whose drills framed the group's stage show. Recruited when Chuck D formed Public Enemy in 1986, he handled press and research and co-wrote "She Watch Channel Zero?!" on It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back (1988). In June 1989, after anti-Semitic remarks in newspaper interviews drew widespread condemnation, Chuck D dismissed him at a Manhattan press conference — SPIN's contemporary feature documents the firing. Griffin then recorded solo, beginning with Pawns in the Game (1990), and rejoined Public Enemy in the mid-1990s. CultureTechLens profiled Professor Griff in Short #176.

name: Paul George
description: Paul George (born Paul Clifton Anthony George, May 2, 1990, in Palmdale, California) is an American professional basketball player, a nine-time NBA All-Star considered among the defining two-way wings of his generation. After two seasons at Fresno State he was drafted 10th overall by the Indiana Pacers in 2010, won the NBA's Most Improved Player award in 2013, and recovered from a severe leg fracture to reach All-NBA First Team level in 2019 with the Oklahoma City Thunder; he later played five seasons for the Los Angeles Clippers before joining the Philadelphia 76ers in 2024. Since 2023 he has hosted Podcast P, the interview show produced with Wave Sports + Entertainment whose record (CTL-E-5596) this graph minted from CultureTechLens Short #84 — a show record that has waited three waves for its host. None of George's four NBA teams yet holds a graph record, so he stages as a documented near-orphan: the host edge itself remains a schema question (see the packet's Gate D table), and his team edges are named, sourced gaps rather than approximations.

name: Pepa
aliases: Sandra Denton; Sandra Jacqueline Denton; Pep; Sandy Denton
description: Pepa (born Sandra Jacqueline Denton in Kingston, Jamaica — reference sources differ on the year, giving November 9, 1964, and November 9, 1969) is the Jamaican-American rapper who, with Cheryl 'Salt' James, formed Salt-N-Pepa in New York in 1985. Raised in Queens and enrolled in a nursing program at Queensborough Community College, where she met James, Denton brought the group its second voice; with DJ Spinderella the trio released Hot, Cool & Vicious (1986), the first album by a female rap act to earn both RIAA gold and platinum certifications, and the breakthrough single 'Push It' (1987). Very Necessary (1993) sold more than five million copies in the United States, and the group won the 1995 Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group. Denton told her own story in the 2008 memoir Let's Talk About Pep. Salt-N-Pepa received the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2021 and were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2025 in the Musical Influence category.

name: PnB Rock
description: PnB Rock, born Rakim Hasheem Allen on 9 December 1991 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, was an American rapper and singer whose stage name joins Pastorius and Baynton, streets in his Germantown neighborhood. He released his debut mixtape in 2014, signed to Atlantic Records in 2015, and broke through with "Selfish" (2016), certified triple platinum by the RIAA. Named to the 2017 XXL Freshman Class, he released the albums Catch These Vibes (2017) and TrapStar Turnt PopStar (2019) and appeared on features including "Everyday We Lit," "Dangerous" and Ed Sheeran's "Cross Me." On 12 September 2022 he was shot during a robbery at Roscoe's House of Chicken 'N Waffles in Los Angeles and pronounced dead at age 30; Atlantic Records confirmed his death the following day.

name: Proviso East High School
aliases: Proviso Township High School; Proviso East; Proviso
description: Proviso East High School is a public secondary school at 807 South First Avenue in Maywood, Illinois, the original campus of Proviso Township High Schools District 209. It opened in 1911 as Proviso Township High School and took the East name in 1958, when the district split its growing enrollment with the new Proviso West High School. The school, whose teams are the Pirates, serves Maywood and the neighboring villages of Broadview, Forest Park, and Melrose Park. Its alumni line runs from astronaut Eugene Cernan and linebacker Ray Nitschke to civil rights leader Fred Hampton and one of the deepest basketball alumni lists in Illinois: the school won its first state basketball championship in 1969, and its graduates include Jim Brewer, Michael Finley, and Glenn "Doc" Rivers, class of 1980, whose jersey is displayed at the school. In the 2010 NBA Finals, three Proviso East graduates — Rivers coaching Boston, Finley playing for Boston, and Shannon Brown playing for Los Angeles — appeared in the same series. Enrollment was reported at 1,663 students for 2024–25.

name: Pras
aliases: Pras Michel; Prakazrel Samuel Michel; Prakazrel Michel
description: Pras, born Prakazrel Samuel Michel on October 19, 1972, in Brooklyn, New York, and raised in Irvington, New Jersey, is an American rapper of Haitian descent, best known as a founding member of the Fugees. He met Lauryn Hill at Columbia High School in South Orange, New Jersey, introduced her to his cousin Wyclef Jean, and the three formed first the Tranzlator Crew and then the Fugees, whose The Score (1996) won two Grammy Awards. His solo debut album, Ghetto Supastar (1998), carried the Grammy-nominated title single with Ol' Dirty Bastard and Mýa, a top-forty hit, as was his 1997 'Avenues.' He later worked in film and television, winning a Daytime Emmy Award in 2017 as a producer of the web series The Bay. In April 2023 a federal jury in Washington, D.C., convicted him on ten counts, including conspiracy involving foreign campaign contributions and acting as an unregistered foreign agent, in the case arising from Malaysian financier Jho Low and the 1MDB scandal. On November 20, 2025, he was sentenced to fourteen years in prison; he has appealed, and in April 2026 he reported to a federal facility in Arizona to begin the sentence while the appeal continues.

name: Professor X
aliases: Lumumba Carson; Baba Professor X the Overseer; Professor X the Overseer; PXO
description: Professor X (born Lumumba Carson on August 4, 1956, in Brooklyn, New York; died March 17, 2006) was the orator and ideological anchor of the Brooklyn hip-hop group X-Clan, billed as Professor X the Overseer. The son of Brooklyn activist Sonny 'Abubadika' Carson, he was a founding member of the group and is featured on nearly every song on its two foundational albums, To the East, Blackwards (1990) and Xodus (1992), his interludes framing Brother J's verses with the benediction that the work was protected by the red, the black and the green. He released two solo albums, Years of the 9, on the Blackhand Side and Puss 'N Boots (The Struggle Continues...) (1993). In his own account, preserved in Brian Coleman's hip-hop history reporting, the Blackwatch crew that became the Blackwatch Movement was his idea — a fan base deliberately built into a movement — while his father led the organization. He died in 2006, at 49, of complications of spinal meningitis, the same year X-Clan re-formed without him. He is a different person from the rapper XXXTentacion (CTL-E-5342); the shared token is a documented false artifact, and nothing in this record wires to it.

name: Pelé
aliases: Edson Arantes do Nascimento; O Rei; Pérola Negra
description: Pelé, born Edson Arantes do Nascimento on 23 October 1940 in Três Corações, Brazil, was a Brazilian forward widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers in history and one of the sport's first global icons. He joined Santos at 15 and debuted for Brazil at 16, then announced himself at the 1958 World Cup, scoring a hat trick in the semifinal against France and two goals in the final against Sweden at age 17. He remains the only player to win three World Cups, lifting the trophy in 1958, 1962 and 1970, and he scored 77 goals in 92 official matches for Brazil, a national record that stood for more than fifty years. At club level he is Santos's all-time top scorer, with 643 goals in 659 competitive matches, before closing his playing career with the New York Cosmos (1975–77). Named Athlete of the Century by the International Olympic Committee in 1999, he later served as Brazil's Minister of Sports (1995–98). Pelé died in São Paulo on 29 December 2022, aged 82.

name: Pete Hill
aliases: John Preston Hill; J. Preston Hill
description: John Preston “Pete” Hill (1882–1951) was, in baseball historian Lawrence Hogan's assessment, the first great outfielder in Black baseball history. Born in Buena, Virginia, and raised in Pittsburgh, the left-handed Hill starred for the Philadelphia Giants (1904–1907), Rube Foster's Leland Giants (1908–1910), and the Chicago American Giants (1911–1918), where he served as Foster's captain and center fielder. A complete player — line-drive hitter, daring baserunner, and a center fielder whose arm and instincts drew comparisons to Ty Cobb — Hill reportedly hit safely in 115 of 116 games during one 1911 stretch, a figure SABR treats with caution. In 1919 Foster sent him to player-manage the new Detroit Stars, where, at thirty-six, he produced some of the finest hitting of his career, then wound down with clubs including the Baltimore Black Sox, retiring in 1925. A 1952 Pittsburgh Courier poll named him the fourth-best outfielder in Negro leagues history. Hill died in Buffalo, New York, in 1951 and lay in an unmarked Illinois grave until researchers located it; he was elected to the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 2006, and the Hall later recast his plaque to correct his first name from Joseph to John.

name: PlaqueBoyMax
description: PlaqueBoyMax, born Maxwell Elliot Dent on 3 April 2003 in West Orange, New Jersey, is an American Twitch streamer, record producer and rapper. The second of three children, he graduated from West Orange High School in 2021, where he played varsity basketball, and took a gap year to stream full time after persuading his parents with a slideshow presentation. He began streaming on Twitch in 2021, building the 5$TAR community around music reactions, gaming and collaborative broadcasts, and his music series In the Booth and Song Wars, in which artists create and judge songs live on stream. He joined FaZe Clan in April 2024 and left in August 2025 to develop his own 5$TAR brand. Signed to Field Trip Recordings, he released his debut solo mixtape, Five Forever, in May 2025. In November 2025 he earned a Grammy nomination for “Victory Lap,” made with Fred again.. and Skepta, and in July 2026 he took part in Kai Cenat's Streamer University.

name: Passing Through
description: Passing Through is a 1977 feature directed, produced, written, and edited by Larry Clark, a leading figure of the L.A. Rebellion, the movement of Black filmmakers who studied at UCLA from the late 1960s through the mid-1980s and built an alternative to Hollywood cinema. The UCLA Film and Television Archive, which holds Clark's filmography, lists Passing Through as his 1977 work and summarizes its story: Eddie Warmack, an African American jazz musician, is released from prison for the killing of a white gangster. Clark's own UCLA biography adds that Warmack refuses to play for the mobsters who control the music industry and seeks out his mentor, the legendary Poppa Harris, and that the film features Horace Tapscott and his Pan Afrikan Peoples Arkestra and was co-written by actor Ted Lange. It was Clark's first feature and his master's thesis film at UCLA, where he completed his M.F.A. in 1977. The film had its world premiere at Los Angeles's Filmex and won the Special Jury Prize at the Locarno International Film Festival. The Library of Congress lists Passing Through, under release year 1977, as selected for the National Film Registry in 2023.
